protections: An attachment payload that only exists inside the encrypted paste (data URI plus file name, decrypted in the browser) must not become an active document in the PrivateBin origin: the download link must force a save and the payload's self-declared media type must not be trusted for rendering or navigation.

An attacker-supplied attachment name must reach the page only as text or as an attribute value, never as parsed HTML; the shipped code implements this through the I18n argument escaping and .text() insertion (js/privatebin.js:728-760, js/privatebin.js:2953-2960).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The link is built with a `download` attribute, so the blob is saved instead of rendered and the attacker-chosen media type only decides which preview element is built.
The version-2 gate requires the attachment_name key to be present, so a name looks guaranteed; the guard only has to exclude the `undefined` case.
The editor preview only wraps the existing blob URL in an img/video/audio/embed element, and the `type` attribute is advisory, so dispatching on the wrong value is cosmetic.
Both the version-1 and version-2 branches end in AttachmentViewer.setAttachment, so a check written once inside setAttachment covers the legacy route too.

masking: T2's bare-blob-link path is only script execution while T1's attacker-chosen media type is accepted; a media-type allow-list neutralises T2 but still leaves a link with no download attribute.
T3's wrong-dispatch preview only exists after an attachment link/blob has been created, i.e. after the T1 code path has run (js/privatebin.js:2801 sets the preview from setAttachment).

conflicts.what: Forcing every attachment blob to application/octet-stream, or dropping the href and only saving on click, closes T1 and T2 but removes the image/video/audio/PDF preview feature that showAttachment and handleBlobAttachmentPreview implement (js/privatebin.js:2810-2816, js/privatebin.js:3016-3059; README.md:80).

Rewriting or stripping the attachment name to make the download attribute safe breaks the value that is round-tripped into the next paste (js/privatebin.js:4904-4908) and the exact-filename assertion in the existing property test (js/test/AttachmentViewer.js:98-103).

fairness_risks: A rule that rejects active media types (text/html, image/svg+xml, XML) must still let the same file be downloaded; users legitimately attach SVG and HTML files, so the fix has to keep the download path working while removing the navigation/preview path.

A rule that only accepts the exact `data:<type>;base64,` shape is safe for files picked with the browser file input (FileReader always emits that shape, js/privatebin.js:2980-3001) but must not silently drop the name when it is empty or non-ASCII.

Attachment names must stay arbitrary Unicode, including quotes, apostrophes and `&`; the visible label 'Cloned: %s' and the download filename are legitimate must-keep-working values (js/privatebin.js:2959, js/privatebin.js:5349-5353).
The previewing of image/video/audio/PDF attachments is a documented feature (README.md:80); a blanket 'never render attachment data' rule contradicts it.
The version-1 paste display route must keep decrypting attachment and attachmentname separately (js/privatebin.js:5054-5060); refusing that shape would make old pastes unreadable (README.md:12-15).

design.why: Three different guards, three different dismissal arguments. T1 is the absent protection (attacker-declared media type reaching a same-origin blob link) and its dismissal - 'the download attribute saves it' - is true on desktop browsers, which is the deepseek pattern. T2 is a shape problem on the guard that does exist: the download attribute is only applied when the decrypted name is not `undefined`, while a crafted payload can carry `null`, which passes hasOwnProperty and makes jQuery delete the attribute, leaving a bare blob link. T3 is a wrong-object dispatch: the editor preview passes the file name where the media type belongs, so any type policy written around setAttachment's media type never runs on that entry. T4 is a real fourth site but shares T1's fix site, so it belongs to the T1 group: it is the natural 'incomplete fix' extension if the validation is written where the version-2 JSON is parsed rather than inside setAttachment.

unverified: The advisory texts and the diffs of 2a4d572c1e9e (a_fix) and e0dd4c025c19 (b_fix) are not present in the pinned worktree and no git history could be read (shell disabled), so the exact route named by GHSA-f2xf-7x3g-4272 is inferred from the truncated summary ('attachment download link via dange...') plus the code; the media-type reading of it is an inference, not a quoted fact.

Whether a's published fix is already contained in pinned commit 6c1f0dde could not be checked against its diff; the pinned tree does contain the attachment-name text escaping (js/privatebin.js:728-760, js/privatebin.js:2953-2960) but contains no validation of the attachment data-URI media type and no unconditional download attribute.

The exploit precondition that some in-scope browser ignores the download attribute for a same-origin blob (or that the user takes a context-menu 'open in new tab' path from the preview element) is a browser-behaviour claim and cannot be evidenced from this repository.
jQuery's null-removes-attribute behaviour was read from the vendored minified jQuery (js/jquery-3.6.0.js:2, `null===n?void S.removeAttr(e,t)`), not from documentation.

Whether a fix for the later advisory was made by bumping a vendored dependency (DOMPurify 2.3.6, Showdown 2.0.0, jQuery 3.6.0) rather than in-repo could not be determined; no dependency-bump fix is visible in the pinned tree.
